core_obligations: Choose representatives (proof lines 4148-4170): the author replaces K^bullet by a K-flat resolution and f_*K^bullet by a K-injective complex, so that all four objects in the square are computed by explicit complexes.
Compare the two paths (proof lines 4170-4185): with these choices the two composites are given by the same map of complexes, which follows from the definitions of the four arrows and the adjunction.
Conclude (proof lines 4185-4188): since the representatives compute the derived functors, the commutativity holds in D(O_C) for arbitrary complexes.
proof_roadmap: Replace the complexes by K-flat and K-injective representatives.
Compute both composites of the square with those representatives.
Identify them as the same map of complexes and conclude.
difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts the commutativity of a square of functors involving the naive and derived pullbacks and pushforwards along a morphism of ringed topoi (statement lines 4128-4146, with the Xy-pic square delivered verbatim). The proof replaces the complexes by K-flat and K-injective representatives so that all four functors in the square are computed naively (proof lines 4148-4170), compares the two composites with those representatives and finds the same map of complexes (proof lines 4170-4185), and then concludes for arbitrary complexes because the representatives compute the derived functors (proof lines 4185-4188). The non-formal content is the choice of representatives making all four functors explicit. The claim is H2: one representative choice plus one comparison.
